Not a variable. The address is the operand of the BIT instructions at $879E and $8A16, which are there only to skip the two-byte load after them ($A9 $00 is LDA #0). In zero page it is heli_a_x's third byte, which nothing reads through this name.

High bytes of the three voice pointers ($F8, $FA, $FC).

A tune number for the unreached entry at $02E1, which would load X from here before init_tune.
0 keeps play_frame silent; start_tune sets it to 1 once the tune is ready.
For each voice, 1 when it sounds. A voice switched off still reads its data in time.
How many frames one tick of the tune lasts: 3. This is also the first of the driver's variables a tune can write: a data byte of $99 or more, less $99, is an offset from here.
For each voice, the number of frames between swaps of its two pitches: 4.
For each voice, how much lower the high byte of its second pitch is than its first.
For each voice, how many ticks before a note's end its gate is dropped.
For each voice, which control byte is written at that point: 0 picks release_control, anything else wave.
For each voice, the control byte written before the end of a note when release_kind is 0: $41, pulse with the gate still on.
For each voice, its waveform, as a SID control byte without the gate bit: $40, pulse. A new note writes it with the gate bit added.
For each voice, how much a sliding note's pitch falls each frame.
For each voice, non-zero to flip the lowest bit of its pulse width's high byte every frame.
Non-zero to move the filter cutoff every frame.

The filter cutoff's high byte, as last written to $D416.
For each voice (in steps of two), the low byte of where its data starts: where it goes back to at the 0 that ends its data.
The high bytes of the same three addresses, as indexed from here.
For each voice, a counter stepped down each time its data starts again. Nothing reads it.
For each voice, $80 when the note sounding has bit 7 set, a slide down.
The thirteen note lengths in ticks, chosen by a data byte of 1 to 12: 32, 24, 16, 12, 8, 6, 4, 3, 2, 64, 56 and 1.
Low byte of each voice's pitch (in steps of two). Six more bytes hold the second, detuned pitches.
High byte of each voice's pitch, as indexed from here.
Low byte of each voice's second pitch, the one vibrato swaps with the first.
High byte of each voice's second pitch: the first's less detune.
For each voice, frames left before its next swap of pitch.
For each voice, the value of note_count at which the gate is dropped: the note's length less gate_lead.
For each voice, how many more times a $FE byte will go back to mark A.
For each voice (in steps of two), the low byte of mark A, the place a $FF byte marked.
The high bytes of mark A, as indexed from here.
For each voice, how many more times a $FC byte will go back to mark B.
For each voice, the low byte of mark B, the place a $FD byte marked.
The high bytes of mark B, as indexed from here.
For each voice, which of its two pitches is sounding.
For each voice, 1 until it has read a note. It stops a voice whose data is empty from looping for ever within one frame.

The octave of the note being set up, 0-7 from its low three bits; 7 is the top.
For each voice, ticks left of its present note.

The voice being worked on, 2 down to 0.
Frames left of the present tick.
Low bytes of the SID pitch of the twelve notes of the top octave, entries 1 to 12; entry 0 is not used.
High bytes of the same twelve pitches.
For each of eight tune numbers, the offset in tune_pointers of the last of its six bytes.

Three tunes' starting addresses, low byte then high for each of three voices, each one byte before the voice's first data byte. Tune 0: $0575, $071C, $0821. Tune 1: $09E6, $0B0B, $0BF8. Tune 2: $0CF3, $0E12, $0F51. Only tune 0's three voices and tune 1's first lie in tune data; the other five addresses are inside the scenery tables that begin at $0B00.
The last byte of tune 2's pointers, then 30 bytes of zeros where five more tunes' pointers could go.
A copy of each value a tune writes straight to a SID register, by register number. Nothing reads it.
Unreached: loads X from tune_number and falls into init_tune.
Starts tune X: silences the driver, copies the tune's three addresses into the voice pointers and the loop pointers, and sets every voice to read its first byte on the next call.

One frame of music. Every tempo frames is a tick: each voice's note_count goes down; at 0 the voice's gate is dropped and its data read for the next note; at gate_off_at the control byte for the end of a note is written. Every frame, tick or not, the per-frame effects run (frame_effects).

Reads voice data until a note. 0 ends the data: the voice goes back to its start. A byte of $80 or more is a command (voice_command). Otherwise the byte picks a length from durations, and the next is the note: 0 a rest; else bit 7 a slide, bits 3-6 the note 1-12, bits 0-2 the octave. The pitch is set and the voice's waveform written with the gate on.
The 0 that ends a voice's data: its pointer goes back to the address in loop_ptr_lo and loop_ptr_hi.
Steps voice pointer X on by one and returns the byte there.
Takes note Y's top-octave pitch and a second copy with detune taken off its high byte, and shifts both right once for every octave below 7 (shift_pitch).
Halves the 16-bit pitch at pitch_lo, X as many times as octave is below 7.

Data bytes of $80 and over. $FF: the next byte is a count, and here is mark A. $FE: go back to mark A if the count is not 0, taking one off it. $FD and $FC: the same with mark B. Any other: the low seven bits, if under $19, name a SID register and the next byte is written to it; if $19 or over they name a driver variable, counted from tempo, and the next byte is written to that.

Not a variable: the address is the middle of an instruction of voice_command. It has a symbol because BIT $04A9 at $85C3 and $8826 hides a two-byte load in its operand, the trick the game uses to skip an instruction.
read_voice for a voice that is switched off: lengths and commands are followed and the note itself is skipped.

Run every frame for each voice that is on: a sliding note's pitch falls by slide_rate; otherwise every vibrato_rate frames the voice swaps between its two pitches; and pulse_wobble flips the pulse width. Then filter_sweep moves the cutoff.
Writes the voice's second pitch to the SID: X moved on six, then write_pitch.
Writes the 16-bit pitch at pitch_lo, X to the present voice's frequency registers.
Sets the voice's note_count from durations entry A, and gate_off_at to that less gate_lead.

Tune 0, the only tune the game plays, voice 0: it opens with commands that set the filter, the envelope and the voice's waveform, then 170 notes and rests as written, before repeats, to the 0 at $071C.

Then it restores the status-line helicopters and lets the mid-screen helicopters and the street vehicle move.
drop_in's branch for a player who is out of the game: the monster's two sprites are switched off and it is put in state 15, gone.
The masks that switch off each monster's pair of sprites in $D015: $F3, $CF, $3F.

Brings monster X on. The blimp (sprites 0 and 1) crosses from the left with the monster hanging under it (frame $19) until the monster reaches its column in drop_columns; then the monster falls two pixels a frame (frame $1F) to the street at Y $C4 while the blimp flies on and climbs out of sight.
Where the blimp lets go of each monster, in steps of two pixels: $32, $46, $5A.
Three bytes nothing reads. The instruction at $82A7 that would count the first one up is itself called from nowhere.
The number of the sound effect being started, times 8: its offset into sfx_records.
For each SID voice, how long its effect still has to run. start_sound sets it; only update_sound, which nothing calls, counts it down.
The sound effects' own copy of voice_reg: the offset of each voice's registers from $D400.
For each voice, the high byte of its effect's frequency.
For each voice, its effect's control byte: the waveform with the gate bit set.
For each voice, its effect's attack and decay.
For each voice, its effect's sustain and release. The three bytes after the table are not used.
The filter cutoff of the last effect started, shared by the voices. update_sound would lower it each frame.
For each voice, its effect's filter mode.
start_sound keeps the voice number here while X is busy.
start_sound writes $64 here and nothing reads it.
For each voice, what update_sound would add to the frequency each frame.

Starts sound effect A (0-4) on SID voice X (0-2). It gates the voice off, copies the effect's eight bytes from sfx_records into the voice's variables, sets the filter (every voice routed through it, full resonance, volume 15) and writes the voice's control, envelope and frequency. Nothing touches the voice again until the next effect: every effect has a sustain of 0, so each is one burst that dies away by itself.
Unreached: adds one to sfx_unused_count and returns. No call or jump leads here.
update_sound's voice counter.

Unreached: the routine that would keep the effects going. For each voice whose sfx_time is not 0 it counts the time down, adds sfx_sweep to the frequency and lowers the filter cutoff, and when the time runs out gates the voice off. Nothing calls it, so the sweeps and durations in sfx_records are never heard.

The five sound effects, eight bytes each, starting with effect 0's frequency high byte ($1E). Calls to start_sound ask only for effects 0, 1 and 2. Effects 3 and 4, the last a triangle wave where the other four are noise, are never started.
Second byte of each effect's record: its length in frames, 1 for effect 0. Only update_sound would use it.
Third byte of each record: the control register, $81 (noise, gate on) for effect 0.
Fourth byte of each record: the filter mode for $D418, $20 (band-pass) for effect 0.
Fifth byte of each record: the filter cutoff's high byte, $23 for effect 0.
Sixth byte of each record: attack and decay, $0F for effect 0.
Seventh byte of each record: sustain and release, $0B for effect 0.
Eighth byte of each record, the frequency sweep, $1E for effect 0; then the records of effects 1 to 4 in the same order of bytes, and a spare 0.

Where the loader hands over, and where the game restarts for every level and every return to the title. It clears zero page from $02 up, sets the banking, the video bank and the three hardware vectors (NMI nmi_handler, reset reset_rti, IRQ irq_top), stops the CIA timers, clears both screens and the monsters' sprite shapes, sets the colours, and puts the three monsters on the street in state 1. Then level_intro shows the screens before the level or sets the level up, the two helicopters get paths, and start_day brings the monsters on before control falls into main_loop.

One pass of play: read the controls, run each monster's state routine, give a helicopter that has finished its path a new one, send a new street vehicle when vehicle_step is 0, do the pass's drawing and rules in frame_work, then wait for irq_top to change frame_count. frame_work runs the monsters twice more, so each pass moves them three times.
The base run_monster indexes for the low bytes of the state routines. It is the last byte of main_loop's JMP: states start at 1, so the table proper is state_lo.

Low bytes of the fifteen state routines, states 1 to 15: $8513, $8736, $880E, $8914, $893F, $896C, $896D, $8994, $8995, $89B7, $89E3, $8A27, $8BDE, $8BFF, $8C20. The last low byte, $20, is also state_hi's base.
The base for the high bytes of the state routines, indexed by state from 1: $85, $87, $88, then nine of $89, $8A, $8B, $8B, $8C.
Where run_monster goes for a state of 0 or above 15: it changes the border colour and returns. A leftover from testing; no state outside 1-15 is ever stored.

Runs monster X's state routine, by writing its address from state_lo and state_hi into the JSR below. Afterwards, unless the monster is walking off as a human, it animates a wrecked vehicle (wreck_vehicle); a monster in state 1 or 3 with no control pressed goes to state 11, waiting, with its state kept in resume_state; and the monster's picture is rebuilt (build_monster_frame).
Low byte of the JSR run_monster rewrites with the state routine's address.
High byte of the JSR run_monster rewrites with the state routine's address.
State 1, on the street or a roof: walk, jump or punch (walk_or_act), start climbing if up is pressed beside a building (try_climb), then check what is underfoot (check_footing).

At street level (Y $C4 or more) the monster is put exactly on the street. Higher up, footing_under looks at the screen under it: with nothing to stand on it falls (state 12, frame $0C), unless down is held without fire, when it turns round and starts climbing down the wall it walked off (state 3).

With fire held and a direction, a punch (street_punch). With fire alone, a jump: state 5, frame $20, and the two PLAs drop the rest of state_on_foot. Without fire, left or right turns the monster that way, steps its walk animation and moves it 2 units (4 pixels).

If find_building_side finds a wall beside the monster while up is held, snaps the monster onto it (X adjusted and rounded down to a multiple of 4), turns it to face the building and puts it in state 3, climbing, with frame $1B.

Tests whether monster X is in the hole the weak road leaves: weak_road_state is 0, the monster is at street level, and its X is $2C to $43. If so it shows frame 6, is hurt, and carry is set. While the road is whole or missing from the level the routine returns at once with carry as the caller left it (clear, on every path that reaches it).
Steps the walk animation unless on_weak_road has the monster in the hole: walk_count goes 0-15 and the frame is 8 + walk_count / 4, frames 8 to 11.
For a punch from the street, how many rows above the monster's own row (Y / 8) it lands, by punch_dir: 6, 2, 3, 3.
For a punch from the street by a monster facing left, the column it lands on relative to X / 4, by punch_dir: 0, -2, -2, -4.
The same for a monster facing right: -1, 2, 2, 4.
Works out where a punch thrown from the street lands, as punch_row and punch_col, from the monster's position, facing and punch_dir.

Tests each mid-screen helicopter against the punch: if it is on the screen, not already exploding, and its cell is within one row above and one column left of the punch's cell (cell_near_punch), it is sent down path 8, the explosion, from where it is.
Carry set when target_row is punch_row or one less, and target_col is punch_col or one less.
Helicopter A's place as a character cell: target_row = heli_a_y / 8 - 5, target_col = heli_a_x / 4 - 2. Carry set when its X is under 8 or $9E and over, off the screen.
Helicopter B's place as a character cell, as heli_a_cell.
SEC and RTS, shared by several routines as their 'no' answer.

Starts a punch from the street. Left or right punches only the way the monster faces (frame 4, punch_dir 2); pressed the other way it does nothing. Up gives frame $18 and punch_dir 0, down frame 7 and punch_dir 1. The monster goes to state 2 and the punch is tested at once against the other monsters, the street vehicle and the helicopters. A punch from the street never touches a building: only a climbing monster's does (eat_or_damage).
Unreached: frame $16 with punch_dir 3, a punch behind the monster. Nothing branches here.
State 2: the punch pose is held while fire stays down. On release the monster goes back to state 1 with frame 8.

Looks for a building to climb. Fire must be up and up pressed. For each standing building whose roof is above the monster, the column in front of the monster is compared with the building's first and last columns: a match with the first returns $FF in step_scratch (face right), with the last 0 (face left), and carry clear. The building's number goes to climb_building, its edges to climb_left_x and climb_right_x.

Reads the screen character beside the monster, 4 units ahead and 5 rows up, and then jumps straight to the 'yes' exit. The list of tests it jumps over, at $87DA, once refused a climb unless the character was part of a wall.
Unreached since the JMP at $87D7: accepts characters $0C, $0D, $0F, $10, $40, $41, $25-$28, $46, $47 and $53-$73 and refuses the rest.

State 3, on a wall. Fire with a direction is a punch (climb_punch); fire alone lets go, 4 units out from the wall, into state 12. Up and down move 4 pixels a step with frames $1B and $1C by turns. Reaching the street ends the climb (state 1); climbing above the building's roof line steps the monster 8 units over the edge and $18 pixels up, onto the roof in state 1.

Starts a punch from a wall. Left and right give frame $17 and punch_dir 2 when it is the way the monster faces, into the wall, and frame $16 and punch_dir 3 when it is behind it. Up gives frame $19 and punch_dir 0, down frame $1A and punch_dir 1. With down held the monster also slips 4 pixels lower. It goes to state 4.
For a punch from a wall, how many rows above the monster's own row it lands, by punch_dir: 6, 2, 4, 4.
For a punch from a wall by a monster facing left, the column relative to X / 4, by punch_dir: 0, 0, -3, 2.
The same for a monster facing right: -1, 1, 2, -3.
Works out where a punch thrown from a wall lands (punch_row, punch_col) for the punch_dir in Y.

State 4: holds the pose while fire is down. On release it tests the punch against the helicopters and the other monsters and returns to state 3 with frame $1B. frame_work's eat_or_damage is what tests it against the building, on any pass that finds the monster in this state.
State 5: seventeen steps of 2 units the way the monster faces, with the height following jump_dy, then back to state 1 and a check of the footing.
State 6 is an RTS. Nothing sets it.
State 7, punched by another monster on the level: nine steps of knock_dx with frame $1F, each one costing a hit, then state 12.
For each monster, how far each step of a knock-back moves it: 4 or $FC (-4), set by punch_monsters from the way the puncher faced.
State 8 is this RTS. Nothing sets it.
State 9, out of energy: 63 steps showing shrink_frames, a new one every 8 steps, then state 10.
The eight frames of the change back to a human: $20, $21, $20, $21, $22, $23, $22, $23.
State 10: the human walks off one unit a step, the way the monster faced, on frames $24 and $25, until X is $F8 or $A6, both off the screen; then state 15.
State 11, no control pressed: shows frame 0 on the level or $15 on a wall, and still takes hits from the weak road's hole. Any control returns the monster to resume_state with frame 8 or $1B.
Returns non-zero if monster X has any of its five controls pressed.
State 12: every step costs a hit and drops the monster 8 pixels. It lands in state 1 at the street, or on a roof when footing_under finds one.
footing_under's exit for a roof character: the monster is put in state 1 when its Y is 4 or 12 above a multiple of 16. Carry comes back set when the low four bits of Y are 4 or more.

Reads the screen character at the monster's column (X / 4) and row (Y / 8). Characters $09-$0B and $22-$25 go to footing_found; $20, $21, $40 and $41 return carry set; anything else returns carry set only if it is $DF or more.
For each monster, the first of the other two that its punch is tested against: 1, 0, 0.
For each monster, the second of the other two: 2, 2, 1.

A punch with left or right held is tested against the other two monsters (monsters_overlap), the first found taking it. A victim walking off as a human (state 10) is eaten: it goes to state 15 and the puncher to state 14. A victim shrinking or gone is left alone. One standing on the level is knocked back (state 7); in any other state it is dropped (state 12). knock_dx is set from the way the puncher faces.
Carry set when monster Y is close enough to monster X to be punched: no more than 8 units to its left or 16 to its right, and no more than 8 pixels above or below.

A punch with down and fire held that lands on the street vehicle. Shapes $6A, $6C, $72 and $74 are wrecked: bit 6 of vehicle_flags is set and wreck_vehicle takes over. Any other vehicle moving one unit a frame is speeded up to two.
Carry set when the monster is at street level and the vehicle's column (vehicle_x / 4) is punch_col or one less.
Unreached: three instructions that compare A + $18 with vehicle_x. Only the RTS at $8BA5 is used, as wreck_vehicle's early exit.

While bit 6 of vehicle_flags is set, colours the vehicle orange and, whenever the low three bits of frame_count are 0, moves the wreck on one frame through wreck_shapes_l and wreck_shapes_r. After frame 6 the vehicle is parked off screen, the colour set back to 6 and a new vehicle chosen. run_monster calls it after every state routine.
State 13: nine steps through state_13_frames, then back to resume_state. Nothing sets state 13.
The frames state 13 would show: 1, 2, 0, 1, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0.

State 14: 21 steps of chewing, with frames from eat_frames_street if the monster was on the level and eat_frames_wall if it was climbing, then back to resume_state. Nothing else happens: no energy is gained and no points.
State 15: parks the monster at X $C8, off the screen, and writes 0 to its entry in player_state: out of the game.
The frame for each step of eating on a wall: 5 for the first five steps, then $0F, $10 and $11, three steps each at first.
The frame for each step of eating on the level: $0D for the first five steps, then $12, $13 and $14.
The end of state_eat: resume_state becomes the state again and state_step is cleared.
For each monster, the first column of the building it last started to climb, times 4. Nothing reads it.
For each monster, the last column of the building it last started to climb, times 4. Nothing reads it.
collapse_buildings' loop counter, from last_building down.
The first screen column of each of up to eight buildings. setup_buildings fills it from the level's list.
building_left from its second entry, the form setup_buildings uses to clear the entries after the level's last building.
The last screen column of each building: its first column plus its width, less one.
building_right from its second entry, for the same clearing loop.
For each building, the sprite Y that counts as its roof line, from type_top_y. A monster climbing above it steps onto the roof.
building_top_y from its second entry, for the clearing loop.

For each monster, the number of the building it last started to climb. state_climb uses it for the roof line, and collapse_buildings drops whichever monsters have a falling building's number here, climbing or not. It is never reset, so it carries over from level to level.
Monster 1's entry of climb_building, compared by name in collapse_buildings.
Monster 2's entry of climb_building.

What a jump adds to Y at each of its 17 steps: 0, -6, -6, -6, -4, -4, -2, -2, 0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 6. It rises 30 pixels and comes back down 30. Seven more bytes follow that the jump never reaches.
The left sprite's shape for each frame of a vehicle's wreck. Frame 0 is skipped; frames 1 to 6 are $78, $79, $7A, $7C, $7C and $FC, blank.

The right sprite's shape for each frame of the wreck: $79, $BB, $7B, $7D, $7D, $FC. $BB is not a sprite shape at all: it points at $EEC0, inside the text character set, so the second frame's right half is drawn from eight characters of the font.
Picks one of sixteen street vehicles at random: its starting X, its step, and the shapes of its two halves.
The left sprite's shape for each of the sixteen vehicles.
The right sprite's shape for each of the sixteen vehicles, always the left one's plus one.
Where each vehicle starts: $E8, which wraps round to come on from the left, or $AC, off the right edge.
Each vehicle's step: 1 or 2 units a frame to the right from $E8, $FF or $FE (1 or 2 to the left) from $AC.
Low bytes of the addresses of the thirteen entries of move_records.
High bytes of the addresses of the thirteen entries of move_records, all $8D.

Thirteen kinds of helicopter move, three bytes each: X step, Y step and sprite shape. 0 up, 1 left, 2 left and down, 3 up facing the other way, 4 right, 5 right and down, 6 and 7 hover; 8 to 11 stand still showing the explosion shapes $C0 to $C3, and 12 is the blank shape.
Where path 0's pointer starts: the last two bytes of move_records. A path's pointer is stepped on by two before each read, so its first pair lies two bytes after where the pointer starts.

The nine helicopter paths, each a list of pairs (kind of move, number of frames) ending in $FF. Path 0 is: left 140 frames, hover 100, up 50, right and down 40, right 130. Path 8, the last, is the explosion: moves 8, 9 and 10 for ten frames each.
The Y each of paths 0 to 7 starts at. Helicopter B starts $14 higher.
Path 8's starting Y: punch_helicopters stores the helicopter's own Y here so that it explodes where it was hit.
The X each of paths 0 to 7 starts at: $B4, off the right edge, or 0.
Path 8's starting X, the helicopter's own.
Low bytes of the nine paths' pointers into heli_paths.
High bytes of the nine paths' pointers, all $8D.
Called each pass: if helicopter A has finished its path, falls into new_heli_a_path.
Gives helicopter A one of paths 0 to 7 at random.
Starts helicopter A on path Y: sets its path pointer and starting position and reads the first move.

Steps helicopter A's path pointer on two bytes and reads the next pair. $FF marks the path finished; otherwise the move's kind and length are stored and its X step, Y step and shape are written into move_heli_a's operands.

Called by last_irq every frame: moves helicopter A one step of its present move, or fetches the next move when the present one has run out, and passes its Y and its shape plus rotor_phase to nmi_handler.
Helicopter A's X step for its present move.
Helicopter A's Y step for its present move.
Helicopter A's sprite shape for its present move, before rotor_phase is added.
Called by last_irq every frame: moves helicopter B, as move_heli_a.
Helicopter B's X step for its present move.
Helicopter B's Y step for its present move.
Helicopter B's sprite shape for its present move, before rotor_phase is added.
Called each pass: if helicopter B has finished its path, falls into new_heli_b_path.
Gives helicopter B one of paths 0 to 7 at random.
Starts helicopter B on path Y, $14 pixels above the path's starting Y.
Reads the next pair of helicopter B's path, as next_heli_a_move.
Sets cell_ptr to the address of column A, row Y of the screen on display: the screen draw_screen_hi names is the hidden one, and the EOR with $0C gives the other.
Low bytes of 40 times the row number, for the 25 screen rows.
High bytes of 40 times the row number, for the 25 screen rows.
1 while a text screen is up, so that read_inputs reads the real controls for every player; frame_work sets it to 0 in play, when players who have not joined are steered by ai_input.

Fills the five control bytes of each monster. A player who has not joined (player_state $7F) is steered by ai_input while on_text_screen is 0; otherwise monster 0 reads the joystick in port 2 and monster 1 the one in port 1 (read_joystick), and monster 2 the keyboard: comma left, slash right, @ up, colon down and = fire. Last it reads RUN/STOP, Q and the Commodore key. RUN/STOP, once let go, resets the game to the title; the other two are stored and never looked at.
RUN/STOP was down: wait for it to come up, clear level_begun so the title screens show, reset the game (reset_game) and restart at game_start.
A pause loop that waits for the two joysticks' fire lines to differ. It is entered only when pause_flag is not 0, and nothing ever makes it so.
1 while RUN/STOP is down, as read_inputs found it.
1 while Q is down. Written each pass and never read.
1 while the Commodore key is down. Written each pass and never read.
Tested by read_inputs to enter pause_wait. Nothing writes it, so it stays 0. The byte after it is spare.
Reads joystick port X + 1 through $DC00 + X (so X = 0 is port 2) and spreads its five lines into in_up, in_down, in_left, in_right and in_fire for monster X, each 1 when pressed.
Fills colour RAM with 6, blue, and both screens with character 0.
Marks monster X as hit, in hit_flag. apply_damage turns hits into lost energy once a pass.
High byte of the hidden screen, the one being drawn: $F4 or $F8. flip_screens swaps it each pass.
The top four bits flip_screens gives $D018 to show the screen that has just been drawn: $D0 for $F400, $E0 for $F800.
For each building type, what draw_buildings adds to its screen pointer after a row of blocks to reach the start of the next: $48 for a building 8 characters wide, $46 for one 10 wide.
For each building, where collapse_cells has got to in its map, counting down from $3F.
collapse_offset from its second entry, for setup_buildings' clearing loop. The table has room for eight buildings and two spare bytes.
How many blocks wide each of the six building types is: 4, 5, 4, 4, 5, 4.
How many characters wide each building type is: 8, 10, 8, 8, 10, 8.
The height of each building type in character rows, not counting its roof: 8, 14, 10, 6, 10, 12.
How many damaging punches each building type takes before it comes down: 10, 12, 8, 4, 10, 9.
The sprite Y of each building type's roof line: $88, $58, $78, $90, $60, $60. Five spare bytes follow.
For each value of weak_road_state from 0 to 3, the offset into the street rows of the eight characters to draw over the weak stretch: $28 for the open hole, $40 and $38 as it breaks up, $30 whole.
3 while the weak stretch of road is whole, counting down to 0, an open hole, as it gives way; 4 on a level that has none.
The level number, 0 to 19. end_of_pass adds one when every building is down and wraps 20 back to 0.
Low bytes of the screen offset of a building's top row, indexed by its height in character rows: 40 times (21 - height).
High bytes of the same offsets.
High bytes of the six building templates' addresses, all $9A.
Low bytes of the six building templates' addresses: $9A0D, $9A21, $9A49, $9A61, $9A71, $9A8F.
Low bytes of the eight building maps' addresses, 64 bytes apart from $7580.
High bytes of the building maps' addresses. There are only six: maps 0-3 in page $75, 4 and 5 in $76. Indexes 6 and 7, which random_window reaches, read $29 and $32 from the start of skyline_start.
For each level (low four bits), the column of the 79-column skyline that goes at the right edge of the screen: the level's 40-column view of the scenery.
0 when the title screens are still to be shown; 1 once the newspaper screen has been passed, when level_intro goes straight to setting the level up.
level_init's counter for the eight bytes of a name.
The border colour for even and odd levels: 0, black, and 6, blue.

Sets a level up: the names in the status lines, the border colour, the energy colours, empty bullet and window-thing tables, each monster's set of frames, sprite colour and name colour, the two background colours for the level, the level's lists of buildings (written into setup_buildings' operands), the buildings themselves, the nine characters that differ between the two sceneries, silence, clear screens, and the weak road.

The hidden message: when no player has joined (demo_mode set) and the level is $12, level 19, the names in the status lines are taken $18 bytes further on in name_texts, where they read RHONA, I LOVE and YOU.

The rules and drawing of one pass. Game over is tested, the energy colours set, and in demo mode a fire button returns to the title. Then: hits become damage, climbing punches hit buildings, the scenery and the buildings are drawn into the hidden screen, the status lines written, window things and the weak road drawn and the monsters run, falling buildings moved on, the screens flipped and coloured, bullets moved, a window thing spawned, some windows lit, the helicopter fired, the monsters run again, and the end of the level tested.
Unreached: shows the newspaper screen and restarts.

Counts the pass in loop_count and, every sixteenth pass, looks for a building still standing. If there is none the level number goes up (20 wraps to 0) and the newspaper screen leads into the next level.
Unreached: sets level_begun to 1 and restarts.

Swaps the two screens: the one just drawn goes on display and the other becomes the hidden one. Then it colours rows 4 to 24 of the screen now on display, looking each character's colour up in city_colours, forty columns in a loop of 21 unrolled rows. There are two copies of the loop, one for each screen.
The copy of the colouring loop for the screen at $F800. One of its 21 rows is wrong: at $93A5 it reads row 21's characters from $F748, the other screen, where $FB48 is meant.
Wrecks the next row of building A's map as it falls: working back from collapse_offset, one row of blocks a call, every code below $64 has $64 added, which turns it into its ruined form.
Low byte of the address collapse_cells reads a map cell from, set to the building's map.
High byte of the address collapse_cells reads a map cell from.
Low byte of the address collapse_cells writes the ruined cell to, the same map.
High byte of the address collapse_cells writes the ruined cell to.

Sets up the level's buildings, up to seven, from its two lists: for each, the type (a negative type ends the list), first and last column, roof line, strength, size, and a fresh copy of the type's template in the building's map. The copy is always 64 bytes, more than any template holds, so each map ends with the start of the templates after its own. The entries after the last building are cleared.
Low byte of the address of the level's list of building types, set by level_init from level_types.
High byte of the address of the level's list of building types.
Low byte of the address of the level's list of buildings' first columns, set by level_init from level_columns.
High byte of the address of the level's list of first columns.
An instruction of setup_buildings, marked only because the unreached level-setting routine at $B365 writes a byte here by mistake for col_list_lo.
Low byte of the template address setup_buildings copies from.
High byte of the template address setup_buildings copies from.
Low byte of the map address setup_buildings copies to.
High byte of the map address setup_buildings copies to.

Draws every building that still has height into the hidden screen, from its map: one block, two characters by two, for each map cell, starting at the row height_row_lo gives for its height and working down, height / 2 + 1 rows of blocks in all. A building whose strength is gone gets rubble as well (draw_rubble).
Low byte of the address draw_buildings reads the next map cell from.
High byte of the address draw_buildings reads the next map cell from.
Draws one block: its four characters, from the block_chars entry that block_src_lo and block_src_hi point at, into two rows of two at the screen address in block_dst_lo and block_dst_hi.
Low byte of the address of the block's four characters: the map cell's code times 4, plus $3C10.
High byte of the address of the block's four characters.
Low byte of the screen address draw_block writes to.
High byte of the screen address draw_block writes to.
The jump to draw_scenery_alt, taken on levels with bit 2 of the level number set.

Draws the backdrop into the hidden screen, 40 columns of every row, in an unrolled loop with a copy for each screen. Rows 0-12 come from the thirteen skyline rows, taking the 40 columns that end at the level's skyline_start; rows 13-19 are blank; rows 20-22 are three ground rows from the same columns; rows 23 and 24, the street, come from the first 40 columns of the street rows.
draw_scenery's copy for the screen at $F800.

The backdrop for levels with bit 2 of the level number set: three rows of character 1 at the top, the six rows of the second skyline in rows 3-8, blank down to row 18, then four ground rows and the street. This is the copy for the screen at $F400.
draw_scenery_alt's copy for the screen at $F800.
On the second scenery, fills rows 23 and 24 of both screens with character $64 in place of the street.

On levels with the second scenery, fill_street_alt and nothing more. Otherwise, unless the level has no weak road (weak_road_state 4): a monster landing on the weak stretch starts it giving way (weak_road_check); the stretch's eight characters in both street rows are redrawn for its present state; and while it gives way, every fourth pass plays effect 0 and takes weak_road_state down one, until 0 leaves the hole open.
While the road is whole (weak_road_state 3): a monster that is falling (state 12), with Y $AA or more and X from $2C to $43, sets road_breaking.
Where add_100 keeps X, and apply_damage the number of the monster that ran out of energy.
Where add_100 keeps Y.
1 while the weak road is giving way.
Counted up each pass while the road gives way; every fourth count moves it on.
Unreached: five calls of add_100. No call or jump leads here.

Adds 100 to monster X's score. The score is kept as six characters, digits being characters $40-$49; this steps the fourth and carries leftwards, leaving the last two at 0. Its only caller is damage_building, so points come from damaging buildings and from nothing else.
Returns a random byte from seed X (0-3): the seed times 5 plus $15, which is also stored back as the new seed.

Writes the status lines into both screens: each player's name in row 0, score in row 1 and the word in row 2, DAMAGE in play, six characters each at columns 3, 18 and 32. It also sets their colours: the name from slot_name_colour, the score blue, and each letter of the row 2 word from energy_colours.

Lights a window. Takes the next of eight buildings in turn and a random cell of its 64-byte map; if the cell is a dark window half ($2D, $2E, $35 or $36) it becomes the lit one ($59, $5A, $39 or $3A) and carry is clear, otherwise carry is set. There are maps for six buildings only: turns 6 and 7 use addresses built from the wrong table, $2980 and $32C0, which lie in the monsters' frame tables, and a byte there that happens to hold one of the four codes is changed too.
The map of building type 0, four blocks wide: a roof row and four rows of walls and windows, 20 block codes.
The map of building type 1, five blocks wide: a roof row and seven more rows, 40 block codes.
The map of building type 2, four blocks wide: a roof row and five more rows, 24 block codes.
The map of building type 3, four blocks wide: a roof row and three more rows, 16 block codes.
The map of building type 4, five blocks wide: a roof row and five more rows, 30 block codes.
The map of building type 5, four blocks wide: a roof row and six more rows, 28 block codes.
The colour of the first player's name in the status lines, set by level_init from name_colours for the character that player has.
The colour of the second player's name.
The colour of the third player's name.
The sprite colour of each character: 8, orange, for George; 5, green, for Lizzie; $0E, light blue, for Ralph.
The colour of each character's name in the status lines: 7, yellow; 5, green; 3, cyan.
DAMAGE, in the status alphabet (A is character 9). reset_game copies it into status_word_0, status_word_1 and status_word_2.
The first player's word for row 2 of the status lines, eight bytes: DAMAGE in play, OVER once out of energy.
The second player's word for row 2.
The third player's word for row 2.
A space and GAME: apply_damage writes it over the name of a player who has run out of energy.
A space and OVER: apply_damage writes it over that player's status word.
The names shown in the status lines, eight bytes each in the status alphabet: GEORGE, LIZZY and RALPH, then the hidden three, RHONA, I LOVE and YOU, which level_init selects by adding name_offset.
0, or $18 to choose the hidden names (secret_names).
The first player's name as shown in row 0, copied from name_texts by level_init.
The second player's name as shown in row 0.
The third player's name as shown in row 0.

The colours of the first player's row 2 word, a byte a letter: energy_bars makes them all red (2) and then white (1) from the left for as many letters as the player's energy / 8, plus one. With full energy, $38, all six letters are white; they turn red from the right as it falls.
The colours of the second player's row 2 word.
The colours of the third player's row 2 word. Ten spare bytes follow.
The first player's score as six characters ($40 is 0). This first one is the leftmost digit, the last that add_100 carries into.
The second digit of the first score, as add_100 addresses it; with X = 8 or 16 the same instruction reaches the other two scores.
The third digit of the first score, as add_100 addresses it.
The fourth digit, the hundreds: the one add_100 steps first. The two digits after it are never changed from 0.
$FF after the first score, written by reset_game: the end mark for the text printer.
The second player's score, six characters.
$FF after the second score.
The third player's score, six characters.
$FF after the third score, and 30 spare bytes.
Each monster's energy, starting at $38 (56). apply_damage takes 1 for every second hit. Nothing adds to it: the only other writes are 0 and, in reset_game, the starting value.
Monster 1's energy, read by name in energy_bars.
Monster 2's energy, read by name in energy_bars.
For each monster, a count of hits. apply_damage takes energy only when the count comes up even.
For each monster, 1 when something has hit it since apply_damage last ran. However many hits land in a pass, they count as one.
Once a pass, outside demo mode, for each monster in turn (apply_damage_one).

If monster X has been hit: every second hit costs one energy. At 0 the monster, unless already shrinking or walking off, falls first if it is above the street, and on the street starts to shrink (state 9); its name becomes GAME and its status word OVER. A monster already in state 15 has its player_state cleared.
An RTS shared by game_over_check's early exits.
Outside demo mode, if no player is still playing (no player_state of 6): after a pause, shows the instructions screen with the scores, waits, resets the game (reset_game) and restarts at the title.
The outer counter of game_over_check's wait after the instructions screen.

1 while no player has joined: the newspaper screen sets it before it is drawn and clears it when any slot is playing. In demo mode monsters take no damage, a fire button returns to the title, and level 19 shows the hidden names.

Sets the letter colours of the three status words from the players' energy (energy_colours). A slip in the first test: when the first player's energy is 0 it branches past the second player's letters to the third's, so the second player's word stays all red while the first player is out.
Copies nine characters, 72 bytes, into the start of both character sets: chars_scenery_1 on levels with bit 2 of the level number clear, chars_scenery_2 on the others.
Characters 0 to 8 for the first scenery: blank, solid, two diagonals and five skyline pieces.
Characters 0 to 8 for the second scenery. Nine bytes of spare data follow them.
Nine bytes after the two sets of nine scenery characters that nothing reads.
Three bytes, one a player, that level_init and the title screens write and nothing reads.
The second of the three bytes nothing reads.
The third of the three bytes nothing reads, and two spare bytes.
1 once reset_game has run. reset_once would call reset_game again only if it were 0, and nothing clears it.
Calls reset_game if reset_done is 0, which after the first reset it never is.
A new game: all three players not joined ($7F), scores 000000, the status words DAMAGE, level 0, and energy $38 for every monster from start_energy.

The first multicolour background colour ($D022) for each level, by its low four bits. The table holds 15 colours, so levels 15 and 31 would read the first byte of level_colour_2; of the 20 levels only level 15 does.

The second multicolour background colour ($D023) for each level, by its low four bits: 15 colours again, and level 15 reads the first byte of start_energy, $38, of which the VIC uses the low four bits, 8.
The energy each monster starts a game with: $38, $38, $38.
Returns the character at column cell_col, row cell_row of the screen at $F400, leaving map_ptr at the row and Y at the column.
After the scenery and buildings are drawn: draws the window things and the weak road, then runs the three monsters.
Runs the three monsters' state routines, the tail of draw_overlays and of after_draw.

After the screens are flipped: moves the bullets, tries to spawn a window thing, tries up to 21 times to light a window (stopping at the first that lights), lets helicopter A fire, and runs the monsters.

Helicopter A shoots while it flies down a diagonal (move 2 or 5): every second call it fires a bullet from two rows below its cell, down-left on move 2 and down-right on move 5, and plays effect 1 on voice 1. Helicopter B never fires.
Counted down on each call of heli_fire while helicopter A dives; a shot is fired when it is even.

Works out a box of character cells round each monster (two columns wide and three rows tall), then for each of the 32 bullets: draws it, tests it against the three boxes, and moves it one cell in its direction, removing it at the screen's edges. A bullet is drawn by building a character of its own, number $DC plus its slot: the picture of whatever character it is passing over, with a hole cut by bullet_mask and the bullet from bullet_dots put in. Hits are then paid out: a hit monster is hurt and effect 2 plays on the voice with its number.
Low byte of the screen address move_bullets reads the character under the bullet from.
High byte of the screen address move_bullets reads the character under the bullet from.
Low byte of the address of that character's picture in the city character set at $E000.
High byte of the address of that character's picture.
Low byte of the address of the bullet's own character, from bullet_glyph_lo.
High byte of the address of the bullet's own character, from bullet_glyph_hi.
Low byte of the screen address the bullet's character number is written to.
High byte of the screen address the bullet's character number is written to.
The third monster's hit. It sets hit_by_bullet_1, the second monster's flag, where the third's is meant: a bullet that reaches the third monster hurts the second, and the third cannot be shot.
For each monster with a bullet-hit flag set: hurt_monster, and effect 2.
Clears the bullet's slot and goes on with the next.
Where person_fire keeps the window thing's slot number.
Counted down by person_fire; a shot is fired when its low three bits are 0.
A person at a window, called once each time one is drawn: every eighth call the person turns one step clockwise through eight directions and fires a bullet that way from the window's cell.
Unreached: fires a bullet from column 10, row 10. No call or jump leads here.
Puts a bullet in the first free slot, counting down from 31: column X, row Y, life flag A, and the direction in new_dir, 0 to 7. With all 32 in flight nothing is fired.
Unreached: would put window things at eight fixed places taken from the bytes after thing_timer_hi and thing_timer_lo. Nothing calls it.

Draws each of the 32 window things into the hidden screen, but only where the character there is $19 or $E3, a hole a punch has opened. Anywhere else the thing is removed. A thing with a code below $A8 is a person, drawn as character $A0 plus the direction it faces, and one below $A7 also shoots (person_fire); other codes are drawn as they are.
Low byte of the screen address draw_window_things reads.
High byte of the screen address draw_window_things reads.
Low byte of the screen address draw_window_things writes the thing's character to.
High byte of the screen address draw_window_things writes to.

Steps a 16-bit counter and takes thing_codes entry frame_count AND 31. Unless it is $FF, a window thing with that code is put in a free slot at row 7-22 and column 7-38, both taken from the counter's bits. Most land on wall or sky and are removed by draw_window_things on the next pass; only one that falls on a hole stays.
Stores a window thing with code A at column X, row Y in the first free slot, counting down from 31.
For each monster, the column just right of its bullet box.
Monster 1's entry of box_right.
Monster 2's entry of box_right.
For each monster, the row just below its bullet box.
Monster 1's entry of box_bottom.
Monster 2's entry of box_bottom.
For each monster, the first column of its bullet box: X / 4 less 1 or 2.
Monster 1's entry of box_left.
Monster 2's entry of box_left.
For each monster, the first row of its bullet box, three above box_bottom.
Monster 1's entry of box_top.
Monster 2's entry of box_top.
The unreached test_thing's counter, and two spare bytes.
The column of the bullet or window thing being added.
The row of the bullet or window thing being added.
The life flag of the bullet, or the code of the window thing, being added.
The direction of the bullet being added, 0 up and then clockwise to 7.
High byte of spawn_window_thing's counter: its low four bits plus 7 are the row. The eight bytes after it are the rows the unreached test_thing would use.
Low byte of spawn_window_thing's counter: its low five bits plus 7 are the column. The nine bytes after it are test_thing's columns.
For each bullet direction, the low byte of the change in screen address: -40, -39, 1, 41, 40, 39, -1, -41, and 0 for a ninth.
The high bytes of the same changes.
The column step of each bullet direction: 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, -1, -1, -1.
The row step of each bullet direction: -1, -1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, -1.
For each of the 32 bullets, the high byte of its offset into the screen.
For each bullet, the low byte of its offset into the screen.
For each bullet, non-zero while it is in flight.
For each bullet, its direction, 0-7.
For each bullet, its column. A bullet is removed at column 40.
For each bullet, its row. A bullet is removed above row 3 and at row 24. Sixty-four spare bytes follow.
For each of the 32 window things, the high byte of its offset into the screen.
For each window thing, the low byte of its offset into the screen.
For each window thing, its code, 0 for an empty slot.
For each window thing that is a person, the direction it faces, 0-7.
For each window thing, its column.
For each window thing, its row. Sixty-four spare bytes follow.
The type, 0-5, of each building on the level.
How many blocks wide each building on the level is.
How many characters wide each building on the level is. Nothing reads it.
Each building's height in character rows, 0 once it has fallen. A falling building loses a row a pass, and end_of_pass ends the level when all are 0.
building_height from its second entry, for setup_buildings' clearing loop.
Each building's first screen column again, the copy draw_buildings uses.
High bytes of the addresses of characters $DC to $FB in the city character set, one for each bullet slot.
Low bytes of the addresses of characters $DC to $FB.
The eight rows of the mask that cuts a hole for a bullet in the character it passes over.
The eight rows of the bullet itself, ORed into the hole. Five spare bytes follow.

The window things, indexed two ways. spawn_window_thing takes the first 32 bytes: a person, eleven other things ($C0-$C6 and $CD-$D0), then twenty more people ($A0-$A7), $A3 the commonest. eat_or_damage compares the characters a punch lands on with bytes 1 to $24 of the same table, which takes in the five bytes after the 32 as well.
Low bytes of 40 times the row number, 26 rows, for bullets, window things and read_screen_cell.
High bytes of 40 times the row number.
For each of 22 levels, the address of its list of buildings' first columns. Only levels 0-19 are reached; the last two entries repeat level 0's.
The same table from its second byte, the form that fetches the high bytes.
For each of 22 levels, the address of its list of building types, each list ending in $FF.
The same table from its second byte, for the high bytes.
The first columns of the buildings of each level, level after level. Level 0's are 10, 4 and 26.
The building types of each level, level after level, each list ended by $FF. Level 0 is types 0, 1, 2.
The index, in its building's map, of the block damage_building is working on, and two spare bytes.
1 when a bullet has reached monster 0's box this pass.
1 when a bullet has reached monster 1's box, or, by the slip at bullet_hits_third, monster 2's. The byte after it is monster 2's own flag, which is cleared each pass and never set.
The screen row of a building's top, 22 less its height, in damage_building; and level_init's count of names. The byte after it is spare.
The column read_screen_cell reads, and the column of a climbing monster's punch.
The row read_screen_cell reads, and the row of a climbing monster's punch.
The column, in blocks, of the punched cell within its building. Three spare bytes follow.
How many rows above the monster's row a climbing punch is tested against the screen, by punch_dir: 6, 2, 3, 2, with one more taken off before the read.
The column of that test relative to X / 4 for a monster facing left, by punch_dir: 0, -2, -5, 3.
wall_punch_cols_l's counterpart for a monster facing right: -1, 1, 2, -3.
A counter stepped twice a pass and kept to 0-7. Nothing uses its value.
Once a pass: steps pass_turn, then tests each monster's punch against the buildings (eat_or_damage).

For a monster in state 4, a climbing punch. It works out the screen cell the punch lands on and reads three characters there from the screen at $F400. If any of them is in thing_codes the monster starts to eat (state 14). The read was meant to cover a square of four characters: after adding 39 to reach the row below, the sum is never moved into Y, so the 'row below' character is the second one again and the fourth is the next along the same row. The routine then goes on to damage_building whether or not anything was eaten.

Finds the building whose columns hold the punch (one more column to the right for a monster facing right), and the block of its map under the punch. damage_code gives what the block becomes: $FF, nothing; a value with bit 7 set, the broken form of the block; otherwise a hole, whose code gets bit 1 set if the block above is already a hole (and that one gets bit 0), so the two join. Each change takes one off the building's strength, scores 100 and plays effect 0. The same join with the block below does not work: its pointer, below_ptr, is never given a low byte.
A spare byte before hit_building. Nothing reads or writes it.
The number of the building damage_building is working on.
The row, in blocks, of the punched cell within its building.
The number of buildings on the level, the end of damage_building's search.
Where damage_building keeps the monster's number. Six spare bytes follow, four of them the codes $55-$58.
The code damage_building is about to store for a new hole, with its join bits.

What a punch turns each block code into, 128 entries: $FF for a block a punch does not change (holes, ruins and most roof pieces); a value from $81 to $8A for a window or roof end that breaks; and $00, $08, $10 or $18 for wall pieces that become one of four kinds of hole. A breaking block's new code is $54 plus the low three bits of the value, so $81-$84 give $55-$58 and $87 gives $5B, but $88, $89 and $8A give $54, $55 and $56, not the $5C, $5D and $5E that follow on.
The number of the monster whose punch eat_or_damage is testing, kept for add_100.
The character at the punch's cell.
The character one column right of the punch's cell.
Meant for the character below the punch's cell; it gets the same character as punched_char_1.
The character two columns right of the punch's cell.
Unreached: prints the six bytes at debug_bytes as hexadecimal at fixed places in the top two rows of both screens. A debugging display nothing calls.
Prints A as two hexadecimal digits at offset Y of both screens. Called only from the unreached print_hex_row.
The characters print_hex uses for 0-9 and A-F in the status alphabet, and two spare bytes.
The first of the six bytes print_hex_row would print.
The second of the six bytes print_hex_row would print.
The third of the six.
The fourth of the six.
The fifth of the six.
The last of the six.
The start of a game: shows the COLLECT ITEMS screen, then falls into next_level_screens.
Before every level: sets demo_mode, shows the newspaper screen (which clears demo_mode if anyone is playing), sets level_begun and restarts at game_start, which this time goes on to play.
An RTS nothing reaches, then an unreached fragment that would add one to level_begun and restart.
Called by game_start and again by start_day: with level_begun 0 it shows the screens before play (title_screens); otherwise it sets the level up (level_init).

The screen shown when the game is over: the first tune, the five pictures of its bottom strip, four lines of instructions (two at the top, two in the middle, each letter turned from ASCII into the text alphabet where A is character $23), and under them each character's score in the order George, Lizzie, Ralph. It then waits for fire (wait_fire).
YOU MUST EAT FOOD TO SURVIVE, in ASCII with two spaces before it, the first line of the instructions screen. Thirty characters of each line are printed and spaces are skipped.
CLIMB AND DAMAGE BUILDINGS, in ASCII, the second line.
DESTROY ALL BUILDINGS, in ASCII, the third line.
TO ADVANCE TO NEXT CITY, in ASCII, the fourth line.
Unreached: for each of three scores, compares it digit by digit with the matching entry of high_scores and copies it there if it is greater. Nothing calls it, so the game keeps no high scores.
Operand of the unreached high_score_update: low byte of the high-score address it compares against.
High byte of the high-score address the comparison reads.
Operand of high_score_update: low byte of the score address in the comparison.
High byte of the score address in the comparison.
Operand of high_score_update: low byte of the score address its copy reads.
High byte of the score address the copy reads.
Operand of high_score_update: low byte of the high-score address its copy writes.
High byte of the high-score address the copy writes.
Unreached: prints score X and high score X at the screen places in the four tables after high_scores.
Readies the machine for a text screen: interrupts off, sprites off, display on, and the two multicolour background colours set to yellow and dark grey.
The COLLECT ITEMS screen: asks for the second tune, clears the hidden screen, prints items_text from row 1, column 4, shows it and waits for fire (wait_fire).

Keeps the newspaper screen up for a fixed count of calls of join_screen_tick, 60 turns of an outer counter round a one-byte inner one, about 15,000 calls, however many players join and whenever they do.
Waits for any of the three fire buttons, giving up after some six and a half million tries, then waits for it to be let go.
Reads the real controls and returns non-zero if any player's fire is down.
Unreached: a second random routine, text_seed times 5 plus $7F.

The newspaper screen before each level: asks for the third tune, draws the three strips' pictures and headlines and the line PRESS FIRE TO JOIN THE ACTION in the bottom row, shows it, and runs join_wait.

Prints a three-line headline in each strip. A player who is out (player_state 0) gets the CURED headline; one not joined gets READY FOR ACTION; one playing gets one of eight, chosen by the strip number plus the level, EOR 3, AND 7.

Builds the newspaper's list of fifteen pictures from newspaper_pictures, changes each strip's first picture to its character's and, for a player who is playing, its last picture too, clearing demo_mode as it does; then draws them (draw_picture_list).
Draws the pictures listed in picture_list, last to first, each at its place on the hidden screen.
Copies the screen at $F800 to $F400, the one on display, and colours every cell from text_colours by its character.
Prints text from the address in its first operand to the screen address in its second, until $FF. $FE starts a new line by adding line_step to the screen address.
Low byte of the address print reads from.
High byte of the address print reads from.
Low byte of the screen address print writes to.
High byte of the screen address print writes to.

One turn of the newspaper screen. Before level 0 only, up or down on the port 2 joystick moves the three characters round the three players one way or the other, and up or down on port 1 swaps the second and third; the screen is then redrawn eight times over as a delay. A fire button from a player not yet in joins that player (player_state 6) and redraws the screen.
Redraws the newspaper eight times, the delay after the characters are changed round.
Moves the characters round: the first player takes the second's, the second the third's, the third the first's.
Moves the characters round the other way.
Swaps the second and third players' characters.
Draws picture Y, eight characters by eight from $7000 + 64 times Y, at place X of fifteen on the hidden screen.
Low byte of the address draw_picture reads from, set from picture_lo.
High byte of the address draw_picture reads from, set from picture_hi.
Low byte of the screen address draw_picture writes to, set from place_lo.
High byte of the screen address draw_picture writes to, set from place_hi.

Starts a tune and hands the IRQ to music_irq. Its first instruction loads X with 0, throwing away the tune number each caller passed: the COLLECT ITEMS screen asks for tune 1 and the newspaper for tune 2, and both get tune 0.
Writes 0 to all 29 SID registers.
Sets on_text_screen and reads the controls, so that no player is steered by the computer.
The raster handler for the text screens: one call of the music driver a frame, the screen at $F400 with the text character set, next interrupt at line $C8.
READY FOR ACTION, three lines of twelve in the status alphabet, where $FE ends a line and $FF the text.
HINT... WANT TO EAT. WELL PUNCH SLOWER.
HINT... JUMP WHEN YOU SEE DUST CLOUDS.
SPOUSE OF MUTANT FILES LEGAL ACTION.
OVER GROWING CONCERN OVER MEGA VITAMIN.
EXPERIMENTAL VITAMIN HAS ILL EFFECTS, with the P wrong: the third byte is $FB where $18 belongs, so the screen shows character $FB there.
WOMAN FINDS LAKE TO BE RADIOACTIVE.
UNUSUAL FOOD ADDITIVE MAY BE RECALLED.
SUSPECTED.. POLLUTION OF WATER SUPPLY.
...CURED.... GO BACK TO NORMAL LIFE, for a player who is out.
Low bytes of the addresses of the eleven headlines: READY FOR ACTION twice, the eight for players in the game, and CURED.
High bytes of the addresses of the eleven headlines.
Text nothing prints, in the text alphabet: MISS YOU, then CUDDLE WHUMP FLUMP DUNKS.
PRESS FIRE TO JOIN THE ACTION, centred in forty characters, in the text alphabet.
THEN PRESS FIRE, centred. Nothing prints it.
ONE, TWO and THREE in the status alphabet, each ended by $FF, and a table of three addresses for them. Nothing uses either.

The COLLECT ITEMS screen, nineteen lines of 28 in the text alphabet: the heading, then LIGHT BULB OFF, TELEVISION, SAFE and MONEY BAG; CASSEROLE POT, TURKEY, GLASS OF MILK and BOTTLE OF MILK; LIGHT BULB ON, CACTUS and BOTTLE OF POISON, with the characters of each one's picture at the ends of the lines.
The $FF that ends items_text. It is also the address print's operand holds as loaded.
HIGH SCORE in the text alphabet. Nothing prints it.
GAME SCORE in the text alphabet. Nothing prints it.
The newspaper screen's fifteen pictures, five to a strip: 0, $0C, $0C, $0D, 2; 4, $0C, $0C, $0D, 6; 8, $0C, $0C, $0D, $0A.
The instructions screen's fifteen pictures: ten of picture 0, which the screen then clears, and pictures $0F to $13 across the bottom.
The fifteen pictures draw_picture_list is to draw.
draw_picture_list's counter, 14 down to 0.
For each of the three players: $7F not joined, 6 playing, 0 out of the game.
The second player's entry of player_state.
The third player's entry of player_state.
Low bytes of the addresses of the twenty pictures at $7000.
High bytes of the addresses of the twenty pictures.
Low bytes of the fifteen screen places a picture can go: columns 0, 8, 16, 24 and 32 of rows 0, 8 and 16.
High bytes of the fifteen places, in the screen at $F800.
draw_headlines' counter of strips, 2 down to 0.
Low bytes of the three headlines' screen addresses: column 13 of rows 2, 10 and 18.
High bytes of the three headlines' screen addresses.
The outer counter of join_wait, set to 60.
The inner counter of join_wait and wait_fire. The byte after it is spare.
The seed of the unreached text_random.
Which character each player has: 0 George, 1 Lizzie, 2 Ralph. It starts as 0, 1, 2 and join_screen_tick changes it round.
The second player's character.
The third player's character. The byte after it is spare.

What print adds to the screen address at the end of a line: $0C on the COLLECT ITEMS screen, whose lines are 28 long, and $44 for the headlines, twelve long and on every other row. The byte after it is spare.
The place in picture_list of each strip's first picture: 0, 5, 10.
The place in picture_list of each strip's last picture: 4, 9, 14.
join_screen_tick's counter of players, and of its redraws.
The picture that ends the strip of a character who is playing: 3 for George, 7 for Lizzie, $0B for Ralph.

The picture that starts each character's strip: 1, 5, 9. After the three: unused bytes, among them a second copy of the table of addresses for ONE, TWO and THREE, and high_scores, three scores of 000000 each ended by $FF, which only unreached code touches.
Three high scores of six digits, each 000000 in the status alphabet ($40 is 0) and ended by $FF. Only high_score_update and high_score_print touch them, and nothing calls either.
Low bytes of the three scores' addresses, for the unreached high-score routines.
High bytes of the three scores' addresses.
Low bytes of the three high scores' addresses, $B252, $B259 and $B260.

Copies monster 0's picture buffer at $CCA0 into its six sprite shapes at $F280-$F3FF: 288 loads and 336 stores with no loop. Rows 0-20 of the buffer fill the top pair of sprites. Rows 21-37 are lines 0-16 of the middle pair, and rows 42-47 the first six lines of the bottom pair. Because the raster handlers change a sprite's shape a few lines before it has finished being drawn, each later pair also carries the lines that end the pass before it: the middle pair's lines 17-20 repeat rows 17-20, and the bottom pair has rows 34-37 again at lines 13-16 and rows 38-41 at lines 17-20. One load is wrong: at $B556 the fourth byte of row 1 is read from $CCA6, the row's first byte, where $CCA9 is meant.
